cases.issue_title: average() returns wrong result for lists with a non-integer mean
cases.issue_body: average([1, 2]) returns 1 but should return 1.5. Looks like integer division is being used instead of float division in calc.py.

cases.issue_title: clamp() returns wrong value above the upper bound
cases.issue_body: clamp(15, 0, 10) should return 10 but returns 0. Looks like the above-high branch returns low instead of high.

cases.issue_title: product() returns the sum of a list instead of the product
cases.issue_body: product([2, 3, 4]) returns 9 (the sum) instead of 24 (the product). The accumulator starts at 0 and uses + instead of starting at 1 and using *.
cases.notes: Also used by benchmark/baseline.py to demonstrate the baseline-vs-CodeProof gap: a naive, unverified 'baseline' patch for this case looks plausible (renames the accumulator) but doesn't actually fix the bug — only CodeProof's mandatory re-reproduction check catches that.

note: Seed set (3 cases), not the full 20-30 the spec asks for. Each case is a real, deliberate, verified bug with a real test suite — but scaling to a full historical-GitHub-issue benchmark requires running many live-agent evaluations, which this session's actual constraints (Gemini free-tier daily quota, slow install times, no paid Claude credit at time of writing) made impractical to execute honestly. The runner (run_benchmark.py) and comparison (baseline.py) are built to scale to a larger manifest without changes — adding cases is just adding entries here plus a Playbook.
